summary: Market sentiment remains cautiously mixed as geopolitical tensions in the Middle East dominate the macro landscape, with the US-Iran conflict continuing to escalate and directly disrupting global energy flows, evidenced by Strait of Hormuz ship transits collapsing to just three vessels on Wednesday. The UN General Assembly convening next week adds a critical diplomatic dimension, with key agenda items including Iran sanctions, Houthi threat containment, and Taiwan-China tensions that could materially shift US foreign policy positioning under the Trump administration. On the equity side, stocks staged a partial recovery from recent Fed-induced selling pressure, with Intel and Micron leading technology gains, Johnson & Johnson reinforcing its defensive appeal, and defense names like Lockheed Martin attracting attention following new missile reveals and Patriot interceptor production ramp-ups tied directly to elevated conflict demand. The primary risk factors investors are monitoring include sustained oil market uncertainty — with JP Morgan explicitly stating there is no clear endgame for the Iran conflict — alongside a sharp drop in Hormuz tanker traffic that threatens to tighten global crude supply and reignite inflationary pressures. In the short term, markets are likely to remain volatile and headline-driven, with defense and energy infrastructure sectors offering relative resilience, while broader risk appetite hinges on diplomatic outcomes at the UN and any signals of de-escalation between the US, Iran, and their respective regional proxies.
